out_of_scope_observations.observation: writeDaemonState JSDoc claims atomic but uses plain writeFileSync. Real latent defect: daemon may write zero-byte daemon.state.json under SIGKILL. DEFERRED per QA F3 — daemon.state.json criticality is HIGH (daemon won't start if corrupt); bundling its refactor with codex parity doubles cycle risk without serving the user's stated need. Separate follow-up cycle should adopt the same atomicWriteJson utility introduced in this cycle.

BackendFlavor includes 'opencode' as a value alongside 'openclaw'. Generalizing /list flavor enum NOW (M4) reflects what the codebase ALREADY produces — non-codex wrappers already call createSessionMetadata with their flavor; the daemon already receives this metadata via /session-started. No new tagging logic is needed in non-codex wrappers. This is correctness alignment, not future-feature generalization.

On tmpfs / NFS / certain network filesystems, parent-dir fsync may be a no-op. Vitest's default tmp dirs may not exercise the durability code path. Dev technical hint: use OS-native tmp dirs (os.tmpdir() resolving to /tmp on ext4) for fault-injection tests, OR accept that durability is best-effort on the test filesystem and document the limitation.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: codex sessions are invisible to daemon /list by thread id, recovery is /proc-scan-based (indirect), prior regex fixes did not address the structural asymmetry
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Three tid-bind sites in codex code (runCodex.ts:710-713 startThread, resumeExistingThread.ts:35-38 resume, codexAppServerClient.ts:856 internal-reassign) all update server metadata but NEVER call notifyDaemonSessionStarted — the daemon's in-memory TrackedSession is permanently stale. PLUS: no durable per-daemon mapping; persistence.ts:313-314 daemon-state writeFileSync is labeled atomic but isn't.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — codex integration was added without symmetric notify; predates explicit asymmetry awareness. Prior fix 043e3fec addressed a downstream symptom (regex line 767).
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Codex tid arrives asynchronously after happy-cli has already spawned the session and reported it to the daemon. Claude's flow has the same async pattern but solved it via session.ts:112-124 onSessionFound re-notify; codex flow stopped at the server-side updateMetadata and missed the daemon re-notify hook.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Daemon /list (single source of truth for cross-process visibility) never learns the tid. Recovery script cannot use /list and must fall back to /proc/fd scanning, which is fragile (depends on /proc readability) and indirect (no causal link to daemon ownership).
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Codex integration shipped without notify symmetry. UUIDv7 rollover caused 019dd077 regex bug; 043e3fec generalized the regex but did not fix the architectural asymmetry. This cycle addresses the architectural layer.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Round 0: Q1 verified — split notify hook from mapping file is correct. Q2 nuanced — atomic-rename is NOT over-engineering (writeFileSync truncate/write loses durability on crash); flock acceptable defensive design but not strictly required for single-writer-per-daemon. Q3 verified — per-daemon mapping is necessary because /list is in-memory only; mapping schema must include pid+timestamps and validate PID liveness on load. Q4 corrected — process.title is observability-only (NOT recovery SSoT). Q5: resumeExistingThread.ts:35-38 is a THIRD tid-bind site. Round 0 credit: Architect identified codexAppServerClient.ts:828-867 reassignment sites (startThread:821, resumeThread:856). Codex identified resumeExistingThread.ts:35-38 as the actionable wrapper that holds session context for the daemon notify call. Both insights required; neither dismissable. The shared M1 helper wraps the wrapper sites (with session context) not the deep client (no session context).
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Round 0 spec updated with: (1) M1 explicitly lists THREE tid-bind sites including resumeExistingThread.ts; (2) M3 mapping schema includes pid + timestamps + state field; (3) S1 GC sweep explicitly validates PID liveness on load; (4) S3 reframed process.title as observability-only with Linux truncation note; (5) Won't Have list enumerates codex's scope-creep flags; (6) M1 reuses idempotent /session-started — no new daemon endpoint.
